title: Derived reduction of an extension by a divisible sheaf
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with a final object, and let $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ and $R=(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal C}$ be the constant sheaves of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], where $n\geq1$. Work in sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their cohomological derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $B,F$ be abelian sheaves such that $n:B\to B$ is an epimorphism and $n:F\to F$ is a monomorphism. Put $H=\ker(n:B\to B)$, with its natural $R$-module structure, and $\bar F=\operatorname{coker}(n:F\to F)$. Let $S$ be a short exact sequence $0\to B\to M\to F\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], with connecting morphism $\partial_S:F\to B[1]$, the last arrow of its derived short-exact-sequence triangle [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle]. For the derived change of rings $Lq=-\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}}R$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], there are natural identifications in $D(R)$
$$Lq(F)\simeq\bar F[0],\qquad Lq(B)\simeq H[1].$$
Normalize the second identification so that the scalar-extension unit $B\to\operatorname{Res}Lq(B)\simeq H[1]$ is the connecting morphism $\kappa_B$ of $0\to H\to B\xrightarrow{n}B\to0$. Thus $Lq(\partial_S)$ defines a canonical morphism $d_{S,n}:\bar F\to H[2]$ of $D(R)$. For every sheaf map $s:\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}\to F$, let $\bar s:R\to\bar F$ be its reduction. Under the derived scalar-extension/restriction adjunction [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars], the morphism $d_{S,n}\bar s:R\to H[2]$ corresponds to
$$\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{s}F\xrightarrow{\partial_S}B[1]\xrightarrow{\kappa_B[1]}H[2]$$
in $D(\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C})$; in particular it is the Kummer-type connecting image of the extension boundary of $s$. These identifications and morphisms are natural for morphisms of short exact sequences satisfying these hypotheses and for exact inverse-image functors of geometric morphisms of topoi (left adjoints preserving finite limits), with the induced constant-ring identifications. Here $\operatorname{Res}$ is termwise restriction of scalars, and the adjunction has unit induced by $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}\to R$.
